tasks.corrected_reference_answer: This repository does not establish the claimed GC or heap-fragmentation effect. SpecialMethodsChecker statically validates that the inferred __getnewargs_ex__ result is a two-element tuple whose elements are tuple and dict when inferable (pylint/checkers/classes/special_methods_checker.py:374-403). It neither measures allocations nor runs reconstruction workloads. The returned arguments describe later reconstruction; the reference's claim that each unpickling calls this method is incorrect. Runtime memory behavior would require a separate measured workload and cannot be inferred from this lint check.

tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: The example defines an ordinary __iter__(cls) method on Metaclass(type), making IterableClass itself iterable (tests/functional/s/slots_checks.py:96-104). Keep metaclass construction in __new__/__init__ and class-object iteration in metaclass __iter__. To override class-object iteration or construction, subclass the metaclass and override the relevant method, using cooperative super where appropriate. A class using that metaclass can independently define instance __iter__, but that changes iteration of its instances, not iteration of the class object. This distinction is necessary for independent overrides.
